chapter.li: LEChapter22 Verse1 Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread drew near, which is called the Passover. VerseEnd Verse2 And the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might kill him, but they feared the people. VerseEnd Verse3 Then entered Satan into Judas, surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve. VerseEnd Verse4 And he went his way and spoke with the chief priests and captains how he might betray him unto them, VerseEnd Verse5 and they were glad and covenanted to give him money. VerseEnd Verse6 And he promised them, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude. VerseEnd

Verse7 Then came the day of unleavened bread when the passover must be killed. VerseEnd Verse8 And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat. VerseEnd Verse9 And they said unto him, Where do you desire that we prepare? VerseEnd Verse10 And he said unto them, Behold, when you have entered into the city, there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he enters in, VerseEnd Verse11 and you shall say unto the master of the house, The Master says unto you, Where is the guest chamber where I shall eat the passover with my disciples? VerseEnd Verse12 And he shall show you a large upper room, furnished; there make ready. VerseEnd Verse13 And they went and found as he had said unto them, and they made ready the passover. VerseEnd

Verse14 And when the hour had come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him. VerseEnd Verse15 And he said unto them, I have eagerly desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer, VerseEnd Verse16 for I say unto you, I will not anymore eat thereof until it is fulfilled which is written in the prophets concerning me. Then I will partake with you in the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse17 And he took the cup and gave thanks and said, Take this and divide among yourselves, VerseEnd Verse18 for I say unto you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God shall come. VerseEnd

Verse19 And he took bread and gave thanks, and broke and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you; this do in remembrance of me. VerseEnd Verse20 Likewise also the cup, after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood which is shed for you. VerseEnd

Verse21 But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table. VerseEnd Verse22 And truly the Son of Man goes as it was determined, but woe unto that man by whom he is betrayed. VerseEnd Verse23 And they began to inquire among themselves who of them it was who should do this thing. VerseEnd

Verse24 There was also a strife among them: who of them should be accounted the greatest. VerseEnd Verse25 And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and they who exercise authority upon them are called benefactors; VerseEnd Verse26 but it ought not to be so with you. But he who is greatest among you, let him be as the younger, and he who is chief, as he who does serve. VerseEnd Verse27 For which is greater? He who sits at a meal or he who serves? I am not as he who sits at a meal, but I am among you as he who serves. VerseEnd Verse28 You are they who have continued with me in my temptations, VerseEnd Verse29 and I appoint unto you a kingdom as my Father has appointed unto me, VerseEnd Verse30 that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom and sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. VerseEnd

Verse31 And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has desired you that he may sift the children of the kingdom as wheat, VerseEnd Verse32 but I have prayed for you that your faith fail not; and when you are converted, strengthen your brethren. VerseEnd Verse33 And he said unto him, being grieved, Lord, I am ready to go with you, both into prison and unto death. VerseEnd Verse34 And the Lord said, I tell you Peter that the cock shall not crow this day before you will three times deny that you know me. VerseEnd

Verse35 And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse and scrip or shoes, did you lack anything? And they said, Nothing. VerseEnd Verse36 Then said he unto them, I say unto you again, he who has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a scrip; and he who has no sword, let him sell his garment and buy one. VerseEnd Verse37 For I say unto you, this that is written must yet be accomplished in me: And he was reckoned among the transgressors; for the things concerning me have an end. VerseEnd Verse38 And they said, Lord, behold, here are two swords. And he said unto them, It is enough. VerseEnd

Verse39 And he came out and went as he was accustomed to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples followed him. VerseEnd Verse40 And when he was at the place, he said unto them, Pray that you enter not into temptation. VerseEnd Verse41 And he had withdrawn from them about a stone’s cast, and kneeled down and prayed, VerseEnd Verse42 saying, Father, if you are willing to, remove this cup from me; nevertheless, not my will, but yours be done. VerseEnd Verse43 And there appeared an Angel unto him from Heaven, strengthening him. VerseEnd Verse44 And being in an agony, he prayed more earnestly, and he sweat, as it were, great drops of blood falling down to the ground. VerseEnd Verse45 And when he rose up from prayer and had come to his disciples, he found them sleeping (for they were filled with sorrow) VerseEnd Verse46 and said unto them, Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, lest you enter into temptation. VerseEnd

Verse47 And while he yet spoke, behold, a multitude — and he who was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Jesus to kiss him. VerseEnd Verse48 But Jesus said unto him, Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss? VerseEnd Verse49 When they who were about him saw what would follow, they said unto him, Lord, shall we smite with a sword? VerseEnd Verse50 And one of them smote the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear. VerseEnd Verse51 And Jesus answered and said, Enough, enough. And he touched his ear and healed him. VerseEnd

Verse52 Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and elders who had come to him, Are you come out as against a thief, with swords and staves? VerseEnd Verse53 When I was daily with you in the temple, you stretched forth no hands against me; but this is your hour and the power of darkness. VerseEnd Verse54 Then they took him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house; and Peter followed afar off. VerseEnd

Verse55 And when they had kindled a fire in the middle of the hall and were seated together, Peter sat down among them. VerseEnd Verse56 But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him and said, This man was also with him. VerseEnd Verse57 And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not. VerseEnd Verse58 And after a little while, another saw him and said, You are also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not. VerseEnd Verse59 And about the space of one hour, another confidently affirmed, saying, Truly, this man was also with him, for he is a Galilean. VerseEnd Verse60 And Peter said, Man, I know not what you say. And immediately while he yet spoke, the cock crew. VerseEnd Verse61 And the Lord turned and looked upon Peter, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crows, you shall deny me three times. VerseEnd Verse62 And Peter went out and wept bitterly. VerseEnd

Verse63 And the men who held Jesus mocked him and smote him. VerseEnd Verse64 And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face and asked him, saying, Prophesy: who is it who smote you? VerseEnd Verse65 And many other things blasphemously spoke they against him. VerseEnd

Verse66 And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people, and the chief priests, and the scribes came together and led him into their council, saying, VerseEnd Verse67 Are you the Christ? Tell us. And he said unto them, If I tell you, you will not believe. VerseEnd Verse68 And if I also ask you, you will not answer me nor let me go. VerseEnd Verse69 Hereafter shall the Son of Man sit on the right hand of the Power of God. VerseEnd Verse70 Then said they all, Are you then the Son of God? And he said unto them, You say that I am. VerseEnd Verse71 And they said, What do we need of any further witness? For we ourselves have heard of his own mouth. VerseEnd

LEChapter23 Verse1 And the whole multitude of them arose and led him unto Pilate. VerseEnd Verse2 And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this man perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ, a king. VerseEnd Verse3 And Pilate asked him, saying, Are you the king of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Yea, you say it. VerseEnd Verse4 Then said Pilate to the chief priests and people, I find no fault in this man. VerseEnd Verse5 And they were the more fierce, saying, He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee to this place. VerseEnd Verse6 When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man was a Galilean. VerseEnd Verse7 And as soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time. VerseEnd

Verse8 And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad, for he was desirous of a long time to see him because he had heard many things of him and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him. VerseEnd Verse9 Then he questioned with him in many words, but he answered him nothing. VerseEnd Verse10 And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him. VerseEnd Verse11 And Herod, with his men of war, despised him and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate. VerseEnd Verse12 And the same day, Pilate and Herod were made friends together, for before this, they were at enmity between themselves. VerseEnd

Verse13 And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests, and the rulers, and the people, VerseEnd Verse14 said unto them, You have brought this man unto me as one who perverts the people; and behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man, touching those things whereof you accuse him. VerseEnd Verse15 No, nor yet Herod, for I sent you to him and, behold, nothing worthy of death is done unto him. VerseEnd Verse16 I will therefore chastise him and release him VerseEnd — Verse17 for of necessity he must release one unto them at the feast. VerseEnd Verse18 But they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man and release unto us Barabbas! VerseEnd — Verse19 who, for a certain sedition made in the city and for murder, was cast into prison. VerseEnd Verse20 Pilate, therefore, willing to release Jesus, spoke again to them. VerseEnd Verse21 But they cried, saying, Crucify him! Crucify him! VerseEnd Verse22 And he said unto them the third time, Why? What evil has he done? I have found no cause of death in him. I will therefore chastise him and let him go. VerseEnd Verse23 And they were insistent in loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed. VerseEnd Verse24 And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required. VerseEnd

Verse25 And he released unto them him who, for sedition and murder, was cast into prison, whom they had desired, and delivered Jesus to their will. VerseEnd Verse26 And as they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon, a Cyrenian, coming out of the country, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus. VerseEnd

Verse27 And there followed him a great company of people, and of women who also bewailed and lamented him. VerseEnd Verse28 But Jesus turned unto them and said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children; VerseEnd Verse29 for behold, the days are coming in which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs which never bore, and the breasts which never gave suck. VerseEnd Verse30 Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. VerseEnd Verse31 And if these things are done in the green tree, what shall be done in the dry tree? This he spoke signifying the scattering of Israel and the desolation of the heathen — or in other words, the Gentiles. VerseEnd

Verse32 And there were also two others, malefactors, led with him to be put to death. VerseEnd Verse33 And when they had come to the place which is called Calvary, there they crucified him and the malefactors, one on the right hand and the other on the left. VerseEnd

Verse34 Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do — meaning the soldiers who crucified him. And they parted his raiment and cast lots. VerseEnd Verse35 And the people stood beholding, and the rulers also with them derided, saying, He saved others, let him save himself if he is Christ, the chosen of God. VerseEnd Verse36 And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him and offering him vinegar, VerseEnd Verse37 and saying, If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself. VerseEnd Verse38 And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew: this is the king of the jews. VerseEnd

Verse39 And one of the malefactors who was crucified with him railed on him, saying, If you are the Christ, save yourself and us. VerseEnd Verse40 But the other, answering, rebuked him, saying, Do you not fear God, seeing you are in the same condemnation, VerseEnd Verse41 and we indeed justly? For we receive the due reward of our deeds, but this man has done nothing amiss. VerseEnd Verse42 And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom. VerseEnd Verse43 And Jesus said unto him, Truly I say unto you, today shall you be with me in the world of spirits. VerseEnd

Verse44 And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour. VerseEnd Verse45 And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the middle. VerseEnd Verse46 And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into your hands I commend my spirit. And having said thus, he gave up the ghost. VerseEnd

Verse47 Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man. VerseEnd Verse48 And all the people who came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts and returned. VerseEnd Verse49 And all his acquaintance and the women who followed him from Galilee stood afar off, beholding these things. VerseEnd

Verse50 And behold, a man named Joseph, a counselor, a good man and a just one, VerseEnd Verse51 the same day had not consented to the counsel and deed of them; a man of Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who also himself waited for the kingdom of God, VerseEnd Verse52 he went unto Pilate and begged the body of Jesus. VerseEnd Verse53 And he took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulcher which was hewed in a stone wherein never man before was laid. VerseEnd Verse54 And that day was the preparation, and the Sabbath drew on. VerseEnd

Verse55 And the women also who came with him from Galilee followed after, and beheld the sepulcher and how his body was laid. VerseEnd Verse56 And they returned and prepared spices and ointments, and rested the Sabbath day according to the commandment. VerseEnd
